title: Construction of Chiral “Triple-Decker” Nd(III) Nanocluster with High NIR Luminescence Sensitivity toward Co(II)

synthesis.procedure: All reactions were performed under dry oxygen-free dinitrogen using standard Schlenk techniques. Ligand H2L was prepared by dissolving 2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde (20.0 mmol, 3.04 g) in 15 mL EtOH, adding dropwise over 30 min a 20 mL EtOH solution of 4-methylbenzene-1,2-diamine (10.0 mmol, 1.22 g), stirring under reflux for 4 h, filtering, washing the yellow solid with EtOH (3 × 5 mL), and drying at 100 °C for 2 h (yield 2.49 g, 82%). For 1, Nd(OAc)3·6H2O (0.20 mmol, 0.068 g) and H2L (0.20 mmol, 0.078 g) were dissolved in 15 mL MeOH at room temperature, then 1 mL of a 1.0 mol/L EtOH solution of triethylamine was added. The mixture was stirred under reflux for 30 min and filtered. Pale yellow crystals formed after one week by slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate. The main text only states that H2L and Nd(OAc)3·6H2O in refluxing MeOH, followed by diethyl ether diffusion, give 1, without reagent quantities.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature dissolution, then reflux; ligand dried at 100 °C
synthesis.time: 30 min reflux for 1; crystals after one week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk conditions under dry oxygen-free dinitrogen; slow diethyl ether diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; pale yellow crystals by slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate

properties.summary: 1 shows ligand-sensitized NIR Nd(III) luminescence (LMET efficiency 13.8%) and acts as a selective Co(II) luminescence sensor in CH3CN, with KSV 9.96×10^4 M^-1 and LOD 0.97 μM; other tested cations quench much more weakly or slightly enhance emission.
